solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Female holding drink pouches

indicators.note: one thing holding another keeps it inside, so the second word sits within the first

blocks.note: a female first name
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: A woman carrying drinks in bags or pockets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female' is not the usual F or HER here but a whole girl's name, which opens up to take the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsupia is the Latin plural of marsupium, the abdominal pocket in which kangaroos and their kin carry young.

clue.text: Briefly adequate — though variable — increase in sound

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut short and loses its final letter

blocks.note: ample means enough, sufficient
as in 'cheap, if slow': if can mean though
algebra's x, y and z stand for variables

explanation.surface: Someone grudgingly approving a rise in volume that is adequate but inconsistent.
explanation.walkthrough: AMPL(e) + IF + Y. The dash and 'though' look like a concession in the sentence, but 'though' supplies two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To amplify is to make a signal or noise louder, which is raising its volume.

clue.text: Country united after the end of serious earlier rioting

indicators.note: the end of a word is its final letter, and only that one is kept
a rioting crowd is disorder, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: the last letter of serious
the seven letters of earlier, rearranged
people united are as one

explanation.surface: A nation that came together only after an earlier bout of serious rioting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' places the word for united at the end, behind S + the jumbled EARLIER.
explanation.definitionFit: Sierra Leone is a nation on the coast of West Africa, with Freetown as its capital.

clue.text: First-class sort of voting idea regularly netting millions

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is taken
netting something catches it inside a net, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: PR is proportional representation, a type of electoral system
first and third letters of idea
M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent electoral idea that keeps catching millions of votes.
explanation.walkthrough: PR + I(M)E. 'sort of voting idea' reads as one phrase, but the split comes after 'voting'.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime describes the very best quality, as in prime beef, top grade or first rate.

clue.text: Possible spaces for bass, as featured in song

indicators.note: something featured in a work appears inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
qua is Latin-derived for 'as' or 'in the capacity of'

explanation.surface: Where a bass singer might find room, as heard in a song.
explanation.walkthrough: A(QUA)RIA. Bass here is the fish, not the low singing voice that 'song' suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Aquaria are glass tanks in which fish, such as bass, may be kept and displayed.

clue.text: Disreputable person some consider as callous

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of consider, all of as and the start of callous

explanation.surface: A shady character whom certain people regard as unfeeling.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a rogue or scoundrel, someone dishonest or mischievous and not to be trusted.

clue.text: Recall in relation to cars leads to certain embarrassment

indicators.note: the leads of words are their front letters, so only initials are kept

blocks.note: re means regarding, concerning
the Mini is a small British car
initial letters of certain and embarrassment

explanation.surface: Talk about cars leading to some awkward embarrassment.
explanation.walkthrough: RE + MINIS + C + E. 'leads to' looks like a verb joining the parts but marks the initials.
explanation.definitionFit: To reminisce is to recollect and talk fondly about past experiences.

clue.text: Group from London area (close to Barnet)

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so its final letter is used

blocks.note: SE is the London postcode district for the south-east of the city
final letter of Barnet, a north London borough; the run of letters across 'close to' is a coincidence, not a hidden word

explanation.surface: A gang from one part of London, near Barnet.
explanation.walkthrough: London postcodes are lettered by compass point, so SE is a London area.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection or circle of people or things belonging together.

clue.text: Italian team leaving a place in Georgia

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so a letter departs from the word

blocks.note: Atalanta is a Serie A football club from Bergamo
the letter that is taken out

explanation.surface: An Italian football side departing for a city in the American state of Georgia.
explanation.walkthrough: AT(a)LANTA: removing the second A of the club's name leaves the US city.
explanation.definitionFit: Atlanta is the capital and largest city of the US state of Georgia.

clue.text: Engineer locates impure, valuable substance

indicators.note: to engineer is to contrive or construct, so the letters are built into something new

blocks.note: thirteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: An engineer finds a contaminated but costly material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Engineer' reads as the subject of the sentence but is a verb, the signal to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold, silver and platinum are precious metals, prized commodities worth a great deal.

clue.text: Cut through mass of stone and shell of concrete

indicators.note: the shell of a word is its outside, so only its outer letters are kept

blocks.note: a pier is a solid masonry support, as between arches
first and last letters of concrete

explanation.surface: Drilling through a block of stone and a concrete casing.
explanation.walkthrough: A pier in architecture is a solid pillar of masonry bearing a load, not only a seaside jetty.
explanation.definitionFit: To pierce is to make a hole by penetrating something with a sharp point.

clue.text: Changing tags in German, somehow

indicators.note: somehow means in some unspecified way, so the letters are put in some other order

blocks.note: eight letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Relabelling items in German, by some method or other.
explanation.definitionFit: Renaming means giving something a different label or title, so altering what it is called.

clue.text: Fabricate nasty material to hide universal truth

indicators.note: to hide something is to conceal it inside, so the following pieces go within

blocks.note: manure is dung, unpleasant stuff spread on fields
U is the film classification for universal viewing
a fact is a true thing

explanation.surface: Make up some unpleasant substance to conceal a truth that applies everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: MAN(U + FACT)URE. 'nasty' looks like an anagram signal but is part of the description of dung.
explanation.definitionFit: To manufacture can mean to invent or concoct falsely, as in manufacturing evidence.

clue.text: Many labels come undone, certainly

indicators.note: things that come undone fall apart and can be put back together differently

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Lots of stickers peeling off, without any doubt.
explanation.definitionFit: By all means is a phrase of permission or agreement, equivalent to of course or surely.

clue.text: To avoid disagreement, I had sounded confused

indicators.note: sounded means spoken, so the words are judged by how they are pronounced

blocks.note: to avoid is to miss, a disagreement is a tiff, and I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone explains that, having sidestepped a quarrel, they came across as baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: A tiff is a minor quarrel; 'miss tiff I'd' run together is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Mystified means utterly puzzled or bewildered by something beyond understanding.

clue.text: Old shipbuilder’s failure to respond to doctor?

blocks.note: a refusal or failure: no
the sound a patient makes when the doctor says open wide

explanation.surface: An ancient boatbuilder failing to answer the doctor's question.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is a patient who will not say 'ah' for the doctor, which gives NO + AH.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis, Noah built the ark to survive the Flood, making him the Bible's famous early boat maker.

clue.text: Drive away from the entrance to Sutton Hoo

indicators.note: the entrance to a word is its first letter, so only that one is used

blocks.note: first letter of Sutton
taken as written

explanation.surface: Chasing someone off the gate of Sutton Hoo, the Anglo-Saxon burial site in Suffolk.
explanation.walkthrough: Sutton Hoo is a famous ship-burial site; the setter splits its name, using only the start of the first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Shoo is a verb meaning to chase off a person or animal, typically with a wave of the hands.

clue.text: Aromatic paste — mostly strong, is it?

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the word's final letter is dropped

blocks.note: hard as in tough, strong
taken as written
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA

explanation.surface: Asking whether a fragrant paste is a bit on the strong side.
explanation.walkthrough: HAR(d) + IS + SA. 'It' meaning sex appeal is a crossword favourite, from the 1920s 'It girl'.
explanation.definitionFit: Harissa is a hot North African chilli paste flavoured with spices such as cumin and coriander.

clue.text: Tiny insect shrivels if disturbed

indicators.note: disturbed things are knocked out of place, so the letters land in a new order

blocks.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A little bug curls up when it is bothered.
explanation.definitionFit: Silverfish are small wingless household insects with silvery scales, often found in damp places.

clue.text: Deride US city that’s disgusting and extremely affluent

indicators.note: extremely here means at the extremes, so only the two end letters count

blocks.note: LA is Los Angeles
the exclamation of disgust
first and last letters of affluent

explanation.surface: Mocking an American city as revolting and very wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely affluent' reads as 'very rich' but means only the ends of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: To laugh at someone is to mock or ridicule them, treating them with scorn.

clue.text: Runs what’s too short, revolting horror film

indicators.note: short means lacking something, so the word loses its last letter
revolting is turning over, so the assembled string is read the other way round

blocks.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for runs
eh is a 'what?' of surprise, plus 's for is
also and too both mean in addition

explanation.surface: Reviewing a nasty horror film that is not long enough.
explanation.walkthrough: R + EH'S + ALS(o), all turned round. 'revolting' looks like a review of the film but signals the reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: A slasher is a genre of gory movie in which a killer stalks and knifes victims.

clue.text: Desk forced open? That is acceptable

blocks.note: pried is the past tense of pry, to lever open
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is
U means upper-class, so socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A desk has been broken into; someone says that is fine.
explanation.walkthrough: U for socially acceptable comes from the 1950s 'U and non-U' classification of upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: A prie-dieu is a narrow kneeling stool with a ledge on top for a book, a prayer desk.

clue.text: Small white ball next to a large canine

blocks.note: in the game of bowls, the jack is the small white target ball
taken as written
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A little white ball lying beside a big dog.
explanation.walkthrough: Bowls is a lawn game where players roll weighted balls towards the jack.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackal is a wild African and Asian dog, a member of the dog family Canidae.

clue.text: Judge uncertain for a moment

blocks.note: J is the abbreviation for judge, as in law reports
iffy is informal for doubtful

explanation.surface: A judge wavering briefly over a decision.
explanation.definitionFit: A jiffy is an informal word for a very short time, an instant.

clue.text: Even having money, this would be a great deal!

definitions.text: this would be a great deal
definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer rather than a synonym

blocks.note: straight as in square, even
flush means well supplied with cash

explanation.surface: Breaking even while rich would be an excellent bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deal' is a hand dealt in poker, not a bargain; a straight flush is five consecutive cards of one suit.
explanation.definitionFit: A straight flush is one of poker's strongest hands, so being dealt it is a superb hand of cards.

clue.text: Staff party set up to follow conclusion of seminar

indicators.note: a word's conclusion is its final letter, the only one kept
in a down entry, set up means placed upwards, so the word reads bottom to top

blocks.note: last letter of seminar
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Employees organising a party after a seminar ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts the reversed party word after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a stick or pole, and a rod is a slender straight stick or bar.

clue.text: French satire, not entirely truthful

indicators.note: not entirely means incomplete, so the final letter is missing

blocks.note: Candide is Voltaire's satirical novel of 1759

explanation.surface: A French satirical work that is not wholly honest.
explanation.definitionFit: Candid means frank and open, saying what one honestly thinks.

clue.text: Fruit always once being primarily wrapped in fabric

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is kept
something wrapped in a covering sits inside it

blocks.note: terry is looped towelling cloth
ay is an archaic word for ever, always
first letter of being

explanation.surface: Fruit that was always once kept wrapped in cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: T(AY + B)ERRY. 'once' marks an old-fashioned usage; ay or aye meant for ever.
explanation.definitionFit: The tayberry is a cultivated cross between a blackberry and a raspberry, developed in Scotland.
